chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sufyan ibn al-Simt, who said:

A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Islam and Faith, 'What is the difference between the two?' But he did not answer him. Then he asked him (again). But, he did not answer him. Then they met in the street and the man had approached the ride to leave. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'It is as if you have approached the ride to leave?' So he said, 'Yes'. So he said: 'Meet me in the house'. So he met him and he asked him about Islam and Faith, what is the difference is between the two.

So he said: 'Islam, it is the apparent which the people are upon – the testimony that there is no god except for Allah Alone, there being no associates for Him, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, and establishment of the Salat, and giving the Zakat, and performing the Hajj of the House, and (observing) Sawm the Month of Ramazan. So this is Islam'.

And he said: 'Faith is the recognition of this matter (Wilayah) along with this (all of the above). So if one acknowledges with it and does not recognise this matter, he would be a Muslim, but would be straying'.

key_terms.صِيَامُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Sawm of the month of Ramadan (fasting)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Islam and Iman in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while Islam comprises the visible pillars of practice, Iman requires the inner conviction of Wilayah (divine guardianship). This distinction underscores the Shia theological principle that outward adherence alone is insufficient for salvation, as one may be a 'Muslim' in name yet 'straying' (*dall*) without the essential knowledge of the Ahl al-Bayt's authority.
